newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk banker agrees with Moody's report on his bank.
newsitem.headline: Turk banker agrees with Moody's report on his bank.

text.p: A senior Turkish state banker said on Thursday a report by the U.S. credit rating agency Moody's reflected the truth about the financial problems faced by state banks in Turkey.
"The Moody's report has translated our feelings," said Candan Karlitekin of the state-run Turkiye Kalkinma Bankasi.
Moody's said on Wednesday Turkey's state development banks were financially weak and urged the government to "recapitalise Turkiye Kalkinma or close it down."
"The opinions in the report are realistic," Karlitekin told Reuters.

He said the bank had launched some measures to rescue itself from financial bottlenecks, caused mainly by overdue loans worth 7.5 trillion lira in principal amount, or a total of 22 trillion lira including interests.

The bank, set up to finance investments mainly in the tourism sector, has suffered from lack of fresh resources to continue its activities and attempts to raise money through bond issues have failed in the past, Karlitekin said.
He said the bank had completed a personnel improvement plan and was considering serious and rapid measures to strenghten the financial makeup and restructure its operation.

"We will not issue bonds to raise money. We will ask the government at the annual general meeting in June to raise the capital to 50 trillion lira," he said. The bank's capital is 10 trillion lira now.

A government official said the subject of the Moody's report had already been considered by the government for the past five years. "It does not bring anything new. It talks about things we already know," he said.
